newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NFI 6 loss widens to PLN 42.3 mln in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Polish NFI 6 loss widens to PLN 42.3 mln in 1996.

text.p: Net losses at Magna Polonia National Investment Fund (NFI No. 6) in Poland's mass privatisation scheme worsened to 42.3 million zlotys last year from 0.8 million in 1995, the fund said in an issue prospectus.
Magna Polonia did not give any specific earnings forecast for this year but said it expected to pay a modest dividend in 1998 and increase the payout from 1998 earnings.
The funds said it planned to spend $4-$6 million this year to raise the capital of and form joint ventures for the firms in which it holds strategic stakes.
Investment would be financed by selling shares in firms in which it has minority stakes.
The fund said it might boost 1997 investment to $10 million or more, but the increase would then require selling shares in firms in which it has a strategic stake.
Under the government's NFI programme, shares in about 500 mid-sized companies are allocated to 15 NFIs run by foreign and domestic management firms.

From May 12 the 26 million Poles who bought a participation unit in the scheme will have the opportunity to exchange it for 15 shares, one in each fund, which are expected to start trade on the Warsaw bourse around mid-year.
Each NFI has 31,026,185 shares. The units lose their validity on December 31, 1998.
